newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 18.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 18. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

An earthquake measuring 6.0 on the Ricther scale jolted Indonesia's capital Jakarta on Monday, sending people scurrying out of high-rise buildings. There were no reports of casualties, but some buildings were reported to have developed cracks.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, plans to make it compulsory for joint ventures and foreign banks in Indonesia to allocate at least 20 percent of their overall credit to small businesses.
President Suharto and Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong have agreed to enhance economic cooperations between the seven members of the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN).

The armed forces faction of the House of Representatives said it already had a candidate for vice president. The armed forces have 75 seats in the 500-member House of Representatives. Indonesians will go to poll stations in the general election scheduled for May 29. Presidential and vice-presidential elections are due next year.
